name: Emeka Volkov-Tanaka
creator: Emeka Volkov-Tanaka
description: Volkov-Tanaka works exclusively in augmented reality layers anchored to specific physical locations throughout GLMZ's Tier 1 and Tier 2 corridors — invisible to the unaugmented, his works overlay the built environment with vast, intricate alternate architectures that reimagine Shelf infrastructure as something living, breathing, and dignified. Unlike most AR artists, he does not use registered anchor platforms, instead hacking location data directly into public BCI firmware updates, ensuring his work reaches anyone with a standard BCI whether they choose to or not. He has never been photographed or interviewed.
cultural_impact: The forced-delivery method of Volkov-Tanaka's work — inserting beauty into viewers' perceptual field without consent — sparked the most substantive public debate about AR art ethics since the medium emerged, while simultaneously giving hundreds of thousands of Shelf residents a momentary experience of their environment transformed.
controversy: The BCI firmware injection method is unambiguously illegal under the Neural Integrity Statutes. Volkov-Tanaka has been charged in absentia three times; his identity remains unknown. The Unclocked movement objects strenuously to any art delivered through BCI hardware manipulation. Some admirers argue the non-consent is the point.
story_hooks: A new Volkov-Tanaka work has appeared that depicts a specific building's interior with photographic accuracy — a building whose interior has never been publicly documented and is owned by a major corponation.
Someone has begun impersonating Volkov-Tanaka's style to deliver AR works containing corporate advertising; the real artist, whoever they are, appears to want this stopped.

A character with a standard BCI receives a Volkov-Tanaka injection and realizes the 'alternate architecture' they're seeing matches blueprints for a structure that doesn't exist yet — but is currently in planning.
